raw_comment:
I noticed that a lot of the inland states have more common and higher levels of droughts. Ohio has the most extreme drought out of all of the states it also has the largest area of the bad drought. all of the states close to the coast don't have very bad droughts. Why do inland states have so much more drought compared to other states, but some don't have any? Why do states that have drought in some parts not have it in other parts of the states? This relates to my communities because Michigan where I live is all over the place with extreme to normal it varys a lot
The thirsty nation: drought coming into the Untied states
